description:
pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:122 imports `use std::borrow::Cow;` at the module top.

However, two field declarations in the `Error` enum write the fully-qualified path:

- Line 181: `reason: std::borrow::Cow<'static, str>,`
- Line 208: `reason: std::borrow::Cow<'static, str>,`

Meanwhile every other use in the file uses the imported short name (`Cow::Borrowed(...)` at lines 1264, 1341, 1356, 1372, 1498, 1504, 1509, 1517, 1525, 1530, 1580, 1596, 1711, 1714).

The `use` statement is doing its job for every constructor site but is silently bypassed for two type-annotation sites. The fix is mechanical: replace the two FQ paths with bare `Cow<'static, str>`.

What goes wrong if it stays: cosmetic inconsistency. A reader sees `std::borrow::Cow` in two field types and may think the module-top `use` is dead. Not a correctness issue but a code-smell signal that the file evolved without one final consistency pass.
title: std::borrow::Cow fully-qualified at rustdoc field types is redundant with use std::borrow::Cow
